title: Retro game and application discovery
summary: Screen focused retro repository searches: add 24 projects.
notes: Personally screened hundreds of repository search results against the catalogue, concentrating on C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows. Reviewed pinned repository trees, documentation and selected source. Original source releases, reverse-engineered reimplementations and independent remakes are identified separately. No binaries or installers executed. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Rust engine reconstruction for the 1993 FMV adventure, using the Mac game files and optionally PC and Sega CD content. Includes parsers for Director, resource forks and movie formats.

Swift/AppKit prototype using extracted Amstrad CPC data; game rules are reimplemented rather than running a Z80 emulator. The author says enemy behavior, scoring and full-game completion are not yet faithful or validated.
Native Rust rewrite using CPC game data, with original Z80 routines run offline to extract caves and other assets. The runtime is not an emulator; fidelity is not established as byte-exact.
Rust rewrite of the CPC game using disk-derived levels and audio. The author notes duplicated first cave entries on the supplied disk and approximated simulation and randomness.
Native Rust game using maps and graphics from the CPC III disk. Author reports shared original engine code with the first game, while physics, timing and full campaign fidelity remain unverified.
Native Rust adaptation using CPC VI disk data and the prior Boulder Dash engine. Two raw cave slots are excluded because their extracted data appear invalid; other simulation differences remain.
Work-in-progress annotated Cybernoid disassembly, built on Derek Bolli’s earlier instruction listing. Adds labels and analysis of graphics, controls and sound; no byte-exact rebuild established.
Native Tomb Raider 1 engine remake with modern rendering and optional visual multiplayer features. It uses game content rather than preserving the original executable as source.
Engine reimplementation of Woody Woodpecker: Escape from Buzz Buzzard Park (2001), using original CD data and reverse-engineered game behavior.

Rust reconstruction of the 2000 Windows game engine using original game assets. The project explicitly says Claude Code performed its reverse engineering and wrote code and documentation under human direction.
Rust reimplementation of Warcraft II Battle.net Edition with early multiplayer and support for its expansion. It specifically does not support the original 1995 DOS edition.
Windows reimplementation of the 1996 Star Trek: Klingon interactive video game player, using original discs. Author lists unimplemented feedback and save-on-quit behavior.
Engine reimplementation for Fallout Tactics using original files and rules ported from the executable. Character creation, multiplayer and other features remain missing.
Shared replacement for Rapture’s 1999 moses.dll and Aaron.dll libraries and Hot Shots arcade framework. Individual game ports are private and not supplied by this repository.
Native engine replacement for the 1998 strategy game Fallen Haven: Liberation Day, using original assets. Single-player is reported playable; network play is unfinished.
Early clean-room Acknex-3 engine reconstruction for Saints of Virtue. Author reports working asset pipeline and a first-person debug slice; full game simulation is unfinished.
Incomplete SDL-based recreation of Sid Meier’s Covert Action engine with reverse-engineering and data parsing. The repository points to a potentially newer GitLab copy.
Analysis of one installed HeroQuest DOS directory, with EXEPACK examination and reconstruction of board layouts from quest data. Documentation and reproducible tools, not game engine source.
Examines the 1989 DOS conversion, its EXEPACK executables and compressed image formats; includes a two-stage Huffman and run decoder and reproduction tools.
Research into one installed DOS game directory, including PCX-based images, room masks and the encoded script. Tools reproduce measurements from user-supplied files.
Documentation of the retail DOS shooter’s executable, archive containers, maps, scripts and ACK-3D engine lineage, with reproduction tools.
Examines the DOS Mega Man game’s packed executable, separate stage code and graphics formats, with tools documenting and decoding the inspected data.
Experimental C++/SDL2 port rebuilding animation, fighting and audio using original Rise 2 game files. Includes asset import and reverse-engineering notes.
Python/Pyxel port of the 1987 Spectrum game, with deterministic replay, state snapshots and headless research tools. The project aims for close behavior but does not establish complete parity.
